title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Marina Gupta
body:
Purpose

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer/status-page communication templates. It is intended to be the canonical reference for engineers, SREs, and support teams responding to production incidents.

Scope

Applies to all public-facing inference services, control plane services, and critical internal services that impact customer request success, latency, or data confidentiality. Non-production environments should follow the same patterns but can use lower-priority communications.

Quick links
- Pager/alerting: PagerDuty (Redwood Production)
- Incident Slack channel: #incidents (ops)
- Status page: status.redwood.ai
- Postmortem template: /confluence/templates/postmortem

1) Incident severity definitions and SLOs

Definitions (use these to triage alerts):
- Sev0 (P0): Major outage or data loss. Entire service unavailable or >90% customer impact. Requires immediate page and exec notification.
- Sev1 (P1): Significant degradation. Large customer impact (>25%), large error rate or critical latency degradation causing product breakage.
- Sev2 (P2): Partial degradation or isolated customer impact; degraded performance or reproducible errors affecting a subset of users.
- Sev3 (P3): Minor issues, operational tasks, or non-urgent degradations.

Target response & update cadence:
- Sev0: page within 1 minute; incident leader assigned <5 minutes; status update every 15 min to internal Slack and every 30 min to status page until stabilized. Exec notification (email + Slack DM) within 10 minutes.
- Sev1: page within 5 minutes; incident leader assigned <15 minutes; update every 30 minutes internally, hourly to status page.
- Sev2: page or notification within 30 minutes; updates every 2-4 hours.
- Sev3: handled in normal working flow; update at incident close.

2) Alerting & initial triage checklist

When an alert fires (automated alert, customer report, or monitoring detect):
1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty immediately.
2. Post a brief message in #incidents with alert summary, time, and any initial observations. Use the incident channel template below.
3. Determine severity using the definitions above.
4. Assign an incident commander (IC) — primary on-call for the service. If primary is unavailable, escalate to secondary.
5. Begin a timeline: record time, source of alert, affected service(s), and initial mitigation steps.

Checklist for IC in first 10 minutes:
- Verify alert correctness (reduce noise, check runbook triggers).
- Identify impact surface (observability dashboards: SLI errors, 95th/99th latency, capacity metrics).
- Decide immediate mitigation (traffic diversion, scale up, rollback).
- Open an incident document (link to Confluence incident page) and set status.
- Notify Support/Customer Success if customers are affected.

3) Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): leads the response, sets priorities, coordinates communication.
- Primary on-call (service): executes runbook steps, investigates root causes, runs mitigations.
- Secondary on-call: backup and handles follow-ups, coordinates cross-service escalations.
- Communications lead: drafts external updates and status page entries. Usually assigned by IC.
- Engineering owner(s): responsible for permanent fix and postmortem.
- Exec liaison: notified for Sev0/Sev1.

4) Runbook template and examples

Every service must have a runbook with:
- Pager rules and escalation path
- Key dashboards and logs locations
- Quick triage checklist (health checks, error logs, common mitigations)
- Step-by-step mitigation steps for common failure modes
- Recovery and verification steps
- Post-incident actions and owners

Example runbook excerpt — API 5xx spike / elevated tail latency:
1. Confirm alert: check prod-error-rate dashboard (last 5m error rate > 5% threshold).
2. Check deployment/recent rollouts (kubectl get deploys, CI/CD releases).
3. If errors correlate with a recent deployment, trigger rollback: ci rollback --service inference-api --to-tag <previous>. Monitor error rate for 5-10 min.
4. If rollout not cause, scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/inference-api --replicas=<+2>. Wait 90s and re-evaluate.
5. Check GPU node health and queue lengths. If overloaded, enable burst capacity or route to lower-cost model variant.
6. If persistent, activate fallback (route to dedicated region or cached responses) and notify customers.
7. Record all actions in the incident document and include timestamps.

Code/snippets and commands (examples):
- kubectl logs -n prod inference-api --tail=200
- curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .
- pd-trigger --incident "Sev1 inference-api 5xx spike"

5) Escalation matrix

- If the primary on-call does not acknowledge within the severity response time, PagerDuty escalates to secondary.
- If no resolution after 30 minutes for Sev1, escalate to service owner and on-call manager.
- For Sev0, automatically page Exec liaison and SRE Director if not acknowledged in 10 minutes.

6) On-call rotations and handoffs

Rotation rules (default):
- Primary on-call: 1 week (Mon 09:00 UTC to next Mon 09:00 UTC).
- Secondary on-call: aligned with primary; different rotation group where possible.
- Weekend rotation: split teams to reduce single-person load (4-day rotations possible for small teams).
- Handoffs: incoming/outgoing must complete a checklist in Confluence and post a handoff note in #incidents with: current incidents, mitigations in progress, scheduled changes, and contactable backup.

Handoff checklist:
1. Confirm no active Sev0/Sev1 incidents. If active, incoming IC must be introduced and briefed.
2. Share pager logs and open tickets.
3. Confirm scheduled maintenance windows or rollouts during shift.
4. Verify access tokens/credentials are valid.
5. Document any ongoing temporary mitigations.

7) Postmortem and RCA process

Requirements by severity:
- Sev0/Sev1: Postmortem draft within 72 hours; public summary and internal RCA within 7 days.
- Sev2: Postmortem draft within 7 days; RCA within 14 days.
- Sev3: Postmortem optional; tag and track repeat issues in triage.

Postmortem structure (required sections):
- Title, date, severity, incident timeline (UTC), impact statement, detection method, root cause summary, contributing factors, mitigations applied, action items (owner + due date), follow-up verification plan, retrospective notes.
- Each postmortem must include a "What we learned" section and at least one measurable action to reduce recurrence.

Action item tracking:
- Create JIRA tickets for each action item with label incident-postmortem and link to Confluence. Owners must update the ticket with progress every 2 weeks until closed.

8) Game days (simulated incidents)

Purpose: validate on-call readiness, runbooks, and cross-team coordination.
- Frequency: quarterly for each platform area; at least one company-wide game day per year.
- Scope: planned scenarios (e.g., model-serving memory leak, cross-region failover, KMS outage).
- Evaluation: measure time-to-detect, time-to-IC-assignment, time-to-mitigation, quality of communication, and follow-up action completeness.

Game day playbook:
1. Publish scenario & player list 72 hours before exercise.
2. Run during a 2-4 hour window; observers record timeline and notes.
3. After-action review within 3 business days; produce game-day postmortem.

9) Status page and customer comms templates

Status page entry template (concise):
- Title: [Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved] – <service> degraded
- Affected components: inference API, model routing, etc.
- Impact: brief sentence describing customer-facing effect.
- Start time (UTC): 2026-02-10T14:23:00Z
- Status: Investigating
- Update cadence: every 30-60 minutes
- Root cause (when known): summary line
- Next update: <time>

External email template (initial):
Subject: Incident affecting <service> — We are investigating
Body:
Hello <CustomerName>,
We’re writing to let you know we are investigating an incident that may affect <service>. Impact: brief description. Our engineering and SRE teams are actively working on a fix. We will provide updates every 60 minutes or as material changes occur. No action is required from you at this time.
Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Inference Team

Internal status update template (Slack):
- [HH:MM UTC] Incident #<id> — Sev1 — <service> — brief summary
- Actions taken: rollback / scale / failover
- Next steps: who is doing what by when
- Need: any blockers or exec assistance

10) Verification, recovery and close criteria

Recovery verification checklist (before closing an incident):
- Error rates and latency within normal baselines for 30 minutes
- No queued retries or backpressure indicators for 15 minutes
- Customer-facing failures resolved or acceptable fallbacks in place
- Permanent remediation on track (owner assigned, ticket created)

Closure steps:
1. IC confirms verification checklist.
2. Communications lead publishes "Resolved" status update with short post-incident summary.
3. Create Postmortem and assign owner(s).
4. Schedule retrospective if action items are high-impact.

11) Metrics and dashboards to monitor

Minimum dashboards every on-call should know:
- Global SLI dashboard: 99/95/50 latency, per-model QPS, error rate by endpoint
- Capacity and GPU utilization dashboard
- Queue lengths and backpressure metrics (inference queue depth, task age)
- Service health (pod restarts, OOMs, process crashes)

Owners and maintenance
- Document owner: Eng SRE (oncall-docs@redwood.ai)
- Review cadence: annual review and after every Sev0/Sev1 postmortem

Contact
For questions or suggested edits, please ping the oncall-docs alias or raise a PR on the runbook repository.
